blocks.content: A template is your design of a post in one size: the layout of texts, images, shapes and icons, colours and fonts. Its fields are filled in when generating - you design a template once and use it many times.
Only you see your templates. Nobody else - neither another administrator nor the system administrator - sees or changes them.

New template: enter a name and a format (presets Instagram, Story / Reels, Facebook / LinkedIn, X, YouTube, Pinterest or a custom size of 100-3000 px). The template is created empty and opens in the editor.

items: Duplicate - a copy in the same format (with its thumbnail).
Duplicate to another format - a copy in another size; elements keep their anchor and offset, so a logo anchored top right stays top right. Then fine-tune it in the editor.
Generate (the button of a card or a click on the preview) opens generating a post from the template; the pencil opens the template in the editor.

blocks.content: Cards show the thumbnail (made when you save in the editor), the name, the format and the date of the last change. Search by name, filter by format (the formats you use are offered) and sort by the date of change, of creation or by name.

A deleted template goes to the trash: Restore, Delete for good, Empty the trash. A template in the trash still holds the library images and fonts it uses - they cannot be deleted until the template is deleted for good.
Templates in the trash are deleted for good after the retention period (30 days by default, Core → Settings → Retention, "JS Creator - trash").

blocks.content: Generating fills a template with real texts and photos and saves the finished post into the chosen folder. On the left is the live preview - exactly what will be made; on the right the form with the fields of the template.

Photos from your computer are processed only in your browser and are never uploaded to the server. Only the finished picture and the text of the post are stored. Use photos of people and works of others only with consent or a licence.

items: The grey text in a field is the sample of the template - it never gets into the output, the field must be filled in.

Highlight: select a part of the text and click Highlight - the preview shows it in the highlight style of the template (colour, bold, background). Another click removes the highlight. In the text a highlight is written **like this**.
The counter shows the length and the limit of the field.
When a text does not fit, the template shrinks it, cuts it with “…” or refuses to generate, as it is set - the field tells you what happened.

Fields of inserted blocks are in the form together with the fields of the template; a key that collides with another field has the name of the instance in its label. A set of templates has its own generating – see Sets.
Photo from the computer: JPG, PNG, WebP (HEIC only in Safari), at most 40 MB. The orientation of a phone photo is applied automatically.
From the library: an image of your Library.
Move the crop by dragging the photo right in the preview (mouse or finger), set the zoom with the slider at the field. Default crop returns the setting of the template.
When a photo is small for its place, the form warns that the output may look blurry.

blocks.content: The text you post with the picture on the social network. It is pre-filled from the pattern of the template - {{key}} is replaced by the text of the field (without the highlight marks). You can edit it; Fill from template sets it again from the current fields. Copy the text of a finished output with Copy text.

items: Choose the folder (the last used one is offered) and optionally a name - an empty name = the name of the template with the date and time.
Generate first shows what is still missing (required fields, too long texts, texts that do not fit).

Then it waits for every font and image - when one cannot be loaded, no output is made (never with a fallback font). Likewise a text with a character the font of the template does not have (e.g. an arrow or an emoji) is refused - the form lists those characters. An optional image field may stay empty; its place in the output stays empty.
The template is drawn in its exact size, the server checks the picture, converts it to the format of the template (PNG / JPG) and saves it.
Open the finished output in Outputs, download it or copy its text. The form stays filled - change the fields and click Generate again for another variant.

blocks.content: An output counts towards the quota of your workspace. A full workspace refuses generating - free some space (delete and empty the trash) or ask the administrator for a larger quota.

cards.title: View
cards.text: js-creator-images-view - the page and the preview.

cards.title: Create
cards.text: js-creator-images-create - Generate.

blocks.content: In the editor you design the layout of a template. What you see on the canvas is what the output will be - the preview and the output are drawn by the same code.

items: Top: back to the templates, name, undo / redo, zoom, grid, guides, safe zone and Save.
Left: adding an element (Text, Image, Grid, Shape, Icon) and the layers - the top layer is first.
Right: Properties of the selected element, Fields to fill in and Template (format, background, output, post text).

blocks.content: The editor needs a screen at least 1024 px wide. The list of templates works on a phone too.

items: A click selects an element, Shift + click adds another; dragging over an empty place selects more elements by a rectangle.
Drag an element to move it. It snaps to the edges and centres of the canvas and of other elements (pink guides), with the grid to the grid. Alt = no snapping.
Handles change the size (Shift = keep the ratio), the round handle on the top rotates the element (Shift = by 15°).
A locked element cannot be picked or moved on the canvas - select it in the layers. A hidden element is not drawn, not even in the output.
Ctrl + wheel zooms, Space + drag moves the view.

blocks.content: Every element is pinned to an anchor - one of 9 points of the canvas (corners, middles of the edges, centre). X and Y are the offset from the anchor. When you copy a template to another format or change its size, the element stays at its corner or edge.

items: Anchor - changes the point the element is pinned to, the element does not move.
Move to the edge - moves the element to the chosen corner, edge or the centre with a margin (e.g. a logo top right 40 px from the edges).
Alignment and distribution: one element aligns to the canvas, more elements to each other; three and more elements can be spread evenly.
Content: a fixed text, or a field to fill in - for a field you type a sample text shown in the editor.
Highlights: select part of the text and click Highlight the selection - the part is wrapped in two asterisks on each side and drawn in the highlight style (other colour, bold, background).
Font: a font of the set or an own font of the library, style, size, line height, letter spacing, alignment, uppercase, colour or gradient.
When the text does not fit: it is shrunk down to the minimum size first, then cut with "…", or generating is refused (by the setting). A warning appears under the canvas.
Effects: outline, shadow and a background box (label) around the text or the whole element.

Image: a field to fill in (chosen when generating, a grey placeholder in the editor), or a fixed image of the library (logo, background). Fit crop / whole, focus, corner radius, circle, border, shadow, colour or gradient overlay, mirror.
Grid: layout (2 side by side, 2 × 2, 1 big + 2 …), gap and corner radius; each cell has its own source - All cells as fields creates a field for every cell.
Shape: rectangle with a corner radius, ellipse / circle or a line; colour or gradient fill, outline (also dashed), shadow.
Icon: from the icon set, colour and line width.

blocks.content: The tab Fields shows the fields to fill in in the order of the generating form: label, key (a changed key is changed everywhere), help, required, for a text its sample, max. length and more lines, for an image the recommended minimum resolution. A field disappears with the last element using it.

The tab Template: format (preset or custom size), background (colour, gradient, image with an overlay), output format (PNG, or JPG with its quality) and the post text - the buttons insert fields, generating replaces them with their values.

items: Insert a block with the button Block on the left – choose from the blocks on the page Blocks. An instance behaves like a layer: anchor, offset, rotation and opacity.
The size of an instance is a scale of the block – the handles and the Width / Height fields keep the ratio of the block; the panel Properties also takes it in per cent.
The content of an instance is not changed in the template – Edit the block opens the block editor and the change shows in every template.
Unpack replaces the instance by independent layers of the template (with its fields); later changes of the block no longer apply to it.

Block from the selection: select layers (no block instances), choose a name – the layers move into a new block and its instance replaces them. The step can be undone (Ctrl+Z); the block stays on the page Blocks.
Fields of inserted blocks are in the panel Fields under the fields of the template (read only) – with the key for the post text pattern.
Save (Ctrl + S) saves the template and makes its thumbnail for the list.
If the template was saved meanwhile in another tab or window, the editor refuses the save and offers to load the current state.
Leaving with unsaved changes asks first.
Without the permission js-creator-images-update the editor is read only.

cards.title: Ctrl + Z / Ctrl + Shift + Z
cards.text: Undo / redo (also Ctrl + Y).

cards.title: Ctrl + C / X / V / D
cards.text: Copy, cut, paste (also into another template), duplicate.

cards.title: Delete, Escape
cards.text: Delete the selection, clear the selection; Ctrl + A selects all.

cards.title: Arrows
cards.text: Move by 1 px, with Shift by 10 px.

blocks.content: JS Creator makes graphics of social network posts from templates you design yourself – no AI. The page Outputs is where the generated posts are saved into your folders and where you download them with the text of the post.
Every account has its own private workspace (folders, outputs, library, fonts). Nobody else sees it – no other administrator, not even the system administrator.
The tree of folders is on the left. All outputs is the top level; folders can be nested up to 10 levels. The tree is shared by every kind of output (images now, videos and GIFs later).

items: New folder – the button above the tree (creates it in the selected folder) or + in the row of a folder.
Rename, Move, Delete – icons in the row (on a computer they show when the pointer is over the row).
You can also move a folder by dragging it onto another folder or onto All outputs.
Names in one folder must differ (upper and lower case count as the same).

blocks.content: A folder cannot move into itself or into its subfolder, and the tree cannot be deeper than 10 levels.

On the right is the path of the selected folder, its subfolders and its outputs as thumbnails with the name, date, size, format and file size. A search looks into the names in every folder (the results show their folder); you can also filter by type and sort by newest, oldest, name or size.

items: A click on a thumbnail opens the detail: the picture, folder, template, size, file size, date and the text of the post with Copy text.
Actions: Download (a file named after the output), Rename, Move, Delete, Generate again (opens generating from the same template).
A finished output cannot be edited - generate a new variant from the template quickly.

blocks.content: Tick the outputs (or Select all) - the selection bar has Download ZIP, Move and Delete. A ZIP holds at most 200 outputs and 500 MB; outputs with the same name get “(2)”.

A deleted folder moves to the trash with all its subfolders and outputs as one item; a deleted output is a separate item. Restore brings a folder back with its content (to the top level when its parent no longer exists; a taken name gets “(2)”) and an output into its folder (into All outputs when the folder is gone). Delete for good and Empty trash delete the files too.

Items of the trash are deleted for good automatically after the retention period (default 30 days, Core → Settings → Retention, “JS Creator – trash”). The trash counts towards the space of the workspace.

blocks.content: The library holds the images, fonts and icons you use in templates. It is yours only – nobody else sees it.

At the top is the usage bar: how much of your quota your files take (trash included). From 80 % it turns amber; at 100 % nothing can be uploaded or generated until you delete files and empty the trash.

Logos, backgrounds and photos for the fixed elements of templates. Upload images opens the file choice (several at once); you can also drop images onto the grid. Allowed are JPG, PNG and WebP up to 15 MB (no SVG for security reasons).

items: The server re-encodes every image: it drops the metadata (EXIF, GPS – where and with what the photo was taken), turns the photo upright and scales it down to 4000 px at most. Transparency of PNG / WebP stays.
A click on the thumbnail opens the image in full size; an image can be renamed and deleted to the trash.
Upload only images you may use – photos of people with their consent, works of others with a licence.
An image used by a template (also one in the trash) cannot be deleted - the application lists the templates using it. Replace it in the templates first, or delete the templates for good.

blocks.content: Font set of the application: 25 families with Czech characters (SIL Open Font License), stored on our server – nothing is loaded from Google or any other external service. The sample sentence shows the look of a font.

My fonts: upload a brand or own font with Upload a font – a TTF, OTF, WOFF or WOFF2 file up to 5 MB, the family name, the weight (100–900) and the style (normal / italic). Every face (e.g. Bold, Italic) is uploaded separately; one combination of family, weight and style can exist once.
A font used by a template cannot be deleted - the application lists the templates using it.
Upload only fonts you may use – the licence of the font must allow its use in graphics.

Icon set (Lucide, ISC licence) for templates – colour and size of an icon are set in the template. Search by the English name. Brand logos (social networks) are not included; if you may use one, upload it as an image.

Deleted images and fonts are in the view Trash of their tab: Restore, Delete for good, Empty the trash. Files in the trash count towards your quota until you empty it; after the retention period (default 30 days) they are deleted automatically.
The settings decide how much space the workspaces have. You do not see the content of the workspaces here – numbers only.
Space for the files of one account (outputs, images, fonts – trash included) unless the account has its own quota. The default is 1024 MB; it is entered in MB (1 to 102 400).
The disk of the server is shared with the database, the backups and the other applications – set quotas with a reserve.

The table shows the accounts with access to the application (permission Show the JS Creator application or the sysadmin role) and the accounts that still have data in it ("no access"): numbers of folders, images and fonts, used space and quota. The pencil sets an own quota of an account, or returns it to the default.
When an account is deleted for good, its whole workspace with every file is deleted too. An account in the account trash keeps its data for now (for a restore).
Audit log of JS Creator: who created, changed, deleted or restored a folder, image or font, emptied a trash or changed a quota, and when.

The rows contain only the kind and the number of an item – never names or content of a workspace, so the log does not reveal what anybody works on. Filter by user, event, module and IP address, export and draw charts.
A set joins templates of different sizes (e.g. a 1080 × 1350 post and a 1080 × 1920 story) that have the same fields. One filling then generates an output in every size at once.

items: New set: enter a name and add templates – search them by name and order them with the arrows (outputs are made in this order). A set has at most 10 templates.
The post text pattern is optional – left empty, the pattern of the first template is used.

Fields with the same key (e.g. title) are filled once for every template. They must have the same kind in all templates – when it is a text in one and an image in another, the set is not saved and the message names the field and the templates. Change the key of the field in one template.
Fields of inserted blocks count too (with the key they have in the form of the template).
Generate on the card of a set opens one form with the united fields. A field is required when any template requires it; a text keeps the shortest length limit.
The preview has tabs – one per format. The crop and zoom of a photo are set for each format separately (switch the tab and drag the photo).
Generate draws and stores one output per template in the chosen folder. The name of an output = the name typed (or the name of the set with the date) and its format, e.g. “Sale – 1080×1350”.
A template of the set that is in the trash is skipped. A template deleted for good disappears from the set.

blocks.content: A deleted set goes to the trash – its templates stay as they are. Restore it, delete it for good or empty the trash; after the retention period (30 days by default) it is deleted automatically.

blocks.content: A block is a reusable group of layers – a logo in a corner, a footer with contacts, a price label. Templates use it as an instance; when you change the block, every template using it changes. Outputs already generated stay as they are.

A block has its own canvas (the size of the block) and a transparent background, so the template shows under it. It can contain the same layers and fields as a template – only no other block (blocks do not nest).

sections.heading: 01. New block and the block editor

items: New block: a name and a size (100–3000 px a side) – the block editor opens. It works like the template editor, only without an output and a post text.
A block can also be made in the template editor: select layers and choose Block from the selection (see Template editor).
Duplicate / Duplicate in another size makes a copy of the block; layers keep their anchors and offsets.
After a block is saved, the thumbnails of the templates using it are drawn again by themselves.
A block can have fields (e.g. the price of a label). They appear in the generating form together with the fields of the template.

When the key of a block field collides with another field (the same key in the template, or a second instance of the same block), it gets a number (price_2) and its label the name of the instance. Use this key in the post text pattern too: {{price_2}}.

blocks.content: A block used by a template (also one in the trash) cannot be deleted – the message names the templates. Unpack or remove it there first, or delete the templates for good. Restore a block from the trash, delete it for good or empty the trash; after the retention period (30 days by default) it is deleted automatically.
